messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — I'm seeing a consistent 95th+ tail on /v1/embeddings/rerank this morning. QPS ~220, but p95 token latency jumps around 380–450ms intermittently.
kevin: Ugh. Any kernel-selection traces? last time it was the int8 fallback for sequences >128.
perf-bot: [automated] profile job #3345 completed: cpu: 8%, gpu: 67%, avg_tokens: 42, kv_hit_rate: 0.72, batch_size_p95: 8
sarah: Can you paste the token-level breakdown? `runtime.token.latency` histograms would help.
maria: Pasting the short dump I grabbed from the profiler:
```
runtime.token.latency.breakdown = {
  decode_ms: 14,
  kernel_select_ms: 120,
  kernel_exec_ms: 90,
  kv_lookup_ms: 6,
  queue_ms: 8
}
metrics: qps=220, p95_token_latency=420
kv_cache: hit_rate=0.71, cold_miss_rate=0.29
model_variant: redwood/reranker-v2-8bit
seq_len_distribution: median=32, p95=180
```
kevin: That `kernel_select_ms=120` is the interesting one. We might be re-running expensive kernel selection for long sequences. If seq_len>128 we hit a different kernel path that calls heuristic routines.
tim: Did we recently change quantization fallback logic? I recall a PR that added an "auto-choose" path for int8 kernels when memory < threshold.
maria: Yes — PR #1982 from last week. It added on-the-fly kernel probing when model size + seq_len > threshold. I can revert locally to test.
alex: Meanwhile we should add a token-level tag in the dashboard: group by `kernel_path` and `kv_hit` so we can see correlation. p95 might be driven by kernel_path==probe.
sarah: Agree. I'll add a small per-route panel: `runtime.token.latency{route="/v1/embeddings/rerank"} by (kernel_path, kv_hit)` and a stacked time-series.
kevin: Also instrument `kernel_probe_count` and probe latency separate metric `kernel.probe.lat_ms`. If it's >50ms and happening for many requests, that's the source.
maria: Reproduced locally with a curl script (shared):
```
# repro loop
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/embeddings/rerank \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $DEV' \
    -d '{"input":"long context...","top_k":16,"vector_dim":768}' &
  sleep 0.02
done
```
perf-bot: Note: when seq_len distribution crosses p95>128, batch sizing heuristics switch to conservative_mode which reduces batch aggregation and can drive higher per-token overhead.
tim: If conservative_mode reduces batching, we should also check effective batch_size metric. Compare `batch.size.effective` before/after the spikes.
maria: I toggled the new probe flag off and re-ran in staging: p95 tokens dropped from 410ms -> 170ms and end-to-end p95 latency improved ~35%.
kevin: Nice. That points straight at the probe path. Long-term: we should cache kernel selection results keyed by (model_sha, quant_profile, seq_bucket) so probe cost is amortized.
sarah: I'll add a dashboard panel showing `kernel_lookup.cache_hit_rate` and a small alert if probe_rate > 1% of requests for >5m.
alex: Also, embeddings rerank is sensitive to batch sizing. Add a histogram of `vector_dim` per request and correlate with `batch.size.effective`. If many clients send dim=512 vs 768, kernel paths might differ.
maria: One oddity — KV cache hit_rate is 0.71 but during spikes it dips to 0.45. Could be polling pattern from a client that disables prefix caching.
tim: Can we tag requests with `kv_disabled=true` in metrics? Then filter dashboard to see only kv_enabled requests.
kevin: I'll drop a small PR to add `metric: request.tag.kv_enabled` and `metric: kernel.path` labels at the API frontdoor so we get consistent labels early in the pipeline.
sarah: Ops question: do we want an automatic fallback to float16 kernel if probe exceeds threshold? That trades a bit of perf for stability.
maria: For now let's enable short-term fallback in Dedicated and a config flag in Private. I'll schedule a canary tomorrow.
alex: I'll make a compact dashboard tile: table with columns [time, qps, p95_token_latency, probe_rate, kernel_probe_ms_p95, kv_hit_rate, effective_batch_size]. That should make regression triage fast.
maria: Thanks team. I'll patch the staging image with probe disabled and run a 1h soak. Will post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: [automated] alert resolved: kernel_probe_rate dropped below threshold
kevin: follow-up: after patch, we saw average effective_batch_size increase from 6 -> 11 and cpu utilization dropped ~12% on the reranker pool.
maria: Staging soak looks good. Moving to canary later today. Will update when canary completes.
